title: Retire the one-off *Probe.java classes under test/benchmark
description: Tool review 2026-09-20 item 12. ixdar-app/test/benchmark holds nine tracked probe classes written to answer one agent's question each (ContractProgressProbe, ContractTimingProbe, DenseSplitAttributionProbe, ExtractionNodeProbe, PatchCoverDriftProbe, SliverPinchProbe, StaleCoverProbe, TwinCellProbe, TwinFloodProbe), several printing '[probe]' lines, and PATCH-111's worktree modifies two of them. The 2026-09-08 ruling was no untracked scratch Java; tracked probes are the same litter one directory over, and they rot as the code under them changes. For each probe: delete it when its question is answered or its subject is gone; turn it into a unit test when it asserts something that must stay true; keep it only when it is a benchmark someone reruns, renamed as a benchmark. ai-workspace's `ixd wt done` now refuses a diff that adds or modifies a test/benchmark/*Probe.java unless the ticket's definition of done names it, so new ones need a stated reason.
definition-of-done:
1. Every *Probe.java under ixdar-app/test/benchmark is deleted, converted to a unit test, or renamed as a benchmark with a one-line Javadoc naming what it measures. 2. No remaining class prints '[probe]' lines. 3. mvn test is green. 4. The ticket's changes-made lists each probe and what became of it.

5. ContractionBenchmark (ContractTimingProbe renamed, with ContractProgressProbe's operator counts folded in) keeps its two [benchmark] log lines: the contraction wall time and fixed-point operator counts are the benchmark's output.
testing-plan: 1. For each probe read its git log and the ticket that added it, and decide delete, test or benchmark. 2. Run the full suite after the change.
changes-made:
Provenance: all nine probes were added in ea9c1d63 (2026-08-15, "correct layout embedding"), the botijo/fertility contraction-churn session; no ticket names them. The session's findings (Ixdar project memory "fan-fixture-diagnostic-landed") record each probe's question, its answer and the fixture test that encoded it. No unit test, main-source class, launch entry or CLI references any of them (only REFACTOR-PLAN-2.md mentions two in prose).
ContractProgressProbe: merged into benchmark/ContractionBenchmark (kept as benchmark). Its operator counts at the fixed point (collapses/patchCollapses/patchSplits) were the contraction's acceptance numbers; the benchmark now reports them from the real `NetworkContraction.contract()` path instead of the per-operator-validated `contractStep()` loop, and a failure's message already carries the counts via `progress()`.
ContractTimingProbe: renamed to benchmark/ContractionBenchmark (kept as benchmark): wall time of the contraction on `-Dbenchmark.off`, used for the 2026-08-15 speed triage (botijo 23.6s -> 3.2s). It now logs `[benchmark]` and rethrows a failure instead of swallowing it, so a broken contraction is a red run.
DenseSplitAttributionProbe: deleted, subject gone. It attributed DenseMeshFewSplitsTest's edge splits to operator steps; TOOL-2 deleted that test on the user's ruling.
ExtractionNodeProbe: deleted, question answered. Node 266's ring-step failure was impostor port matches, fixed by `ExtractedPatchGrids.chainArrivalConsistent` (botijo extraction clean); node 266 is a stale id since the botijo trajectory changed. Open: no unit fixture guards `chainArrivalConsistent`.
PatchCoverDriftProbe: deleted, question answered and already converted. It measured cover-label drift on botijo to learn what a fixture must reproduce; unit.mesh.PatchCoverDriftTest (four torus fixtures, blocked drags asserted) is that fixture test, and NetworkContraction's `[contract]` progress line still reports blocked drags on a real mesh.
SliverPinchProbe: deleted, question answered and already converted. Botijo's collapse-3 sliver-cover tear was root-caused and fixed (label-free ring escape removed from ArcRerouter); SliverPinchFixture + SliverPinchFixtureTest.pinchArcThreadsThePinchAndTheCoversHold is the regression guard. Its hard-coded op count and arc/patch ids are stale.
TwinFloodProbe: deleted, question answered and already converted. Botijo's operator-16 twin-flood (arc 23 landing in the wrong wedge of a merged cell) was fixed by the arrival-wedge pre-ban; MergedCellSlotFixture + MergedCellSlotFixtureTest.baitDragIsBannedFromTheFarWedgeAndTheCollapseFinishesCleanly is the guard. Its hard-coded ids are stale.
StaleCoverProbe: deferred to PATCH-111, untouched. The patch-111 worktree (ZeroArcCollapseOperator rewrite) modifies it; retire it there or after it lands. Until then it still prints [probe] lines, so DoD item 2 is open for this file.
TwinCellProbe: deferred to PATCH-111, untouched, same reason; it still prints [probe] lines.

Verified: ContractionBenchmark on botijo (default) reports the contraction reached its fixed point in 5.195s (collapses=3183 patchCollapses=1564 patchSplits=17). Full suite mvn test: Tests run: 307, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, exit 0. No class outside the two PATCH-111-deferred probes prints [probe] lines (grep over *.java). Launch entry 'TOOL-13: circle-canvas' + tmp/tool-13-circle-canvas.png are the wt done aids; the change has no visual surface. Out of scope, noticed: ixdar-app/test/unit/mesh/DriftLocalizeScratchTest.java is a scratch test in the unit suite that prints [watch] lines and asserts nothing of note.
